body:
Welcome to SPLogbook — an advanced, modern amateur radio logging and station automation environment built in Rust.

1. Initial Setup: Open Help → Welcome Wizard (or Station Profile Settings) to enter your station callsign (e.g. SP6INA), operator name, Maidenhead grid locator (e.g. JO81), and optional CQ/ITU zones.

2. Connecting Your Radio (CAT): Open Settings → CAT / Rotator Setup and choose the backend matching your transceiver (Hamlib rigctld, FLRig, TCI, Icom CI-V, Kenwood, Yaesu, Elecraft, or FlexRadio SmartSDR). Once connected, VFO frequency, mode, and signal reports synchronize in real time.

3. Connecting to a DX Cluster: Open the DX Cluster tab or floating window, select a server preset (e.g. dxcluster.pl:8000, dxfun.com:8000, w3lpl.net:7373), and click 'Connect'. Clicking any DX spot automatically tunes your radio and populates the QSO entry form.

4. Logging a QSO: Enter the correspondent's callsign in the Callsign field and press Enter or F2. SPLogbook immediately resolves the DXCC prefix, calculates bearing and distance, queries online Callbooks (QRZ/HamQTH), and checks award status (ATNO / New Band / New Mode).

Tip: Press Ctrl+Shift+P at any time to open the Command Palette and invoke any application feature from the keyboard.
title: 1. Getting Started

body:
SPLogbook provides the modern NATIVE-CAT async rig control architecture powered by the RigHub multi-radio core and the TxArbiter interlock. It supports 8 dedicated hardware and network backends:

- Hamlib (rigctld): Standard TCP network backend (default port 4532) or background supervisor launching bundled/system rigctld on your serial port.
- Icom CI-V: Direct native binary communication (CI-V $FE $FE ... $FD frames) via serial COM or TCP with auto-address discovery (e.g. 0x94 for IC-7300, 0xA2 for IC-705) and collision backoff.
- Kenwood: Direct native asynchronous ASCII serial CAT (FA, FB, MD, TX, RX, IF commands) with a streaming buffered parser.
- Yaesu: Multi-generational support including CAT-V (5-byte binary frames for FT-817/857/897), ASCII (FT-dx10, FT-991A, FT-710), and CAT-III/IV/IX generations.
- Elecraft: Native support for K2, K3, K3S, KX2, KX3, and K4 transceivers (with serial COM or direct K4 TCP network transport).
- FlexRadio: Native SmartSDR TCP API integration (v2.0–3.x) with slice/meter subscriptions and automatic LAN discovery via UDP broadcast (port 4992).
- FLRig (XML-RPC): Seamless integration with the popular FLRig transceiver control server.
- TCI (Transceiver Control Interface): High-speed WebSocket integration with SDR transceivers (Expert Electronics SunSDR2 PRO/DX, Thetis, ExpertSDR3).

Multi-Radio Core & RF Safety:
- RigHub & TxArbiter: Full dual-rig configuration support (Radio 1 & Radio 2) with a strict transmit arbiter (TxArbiter) enforcing a Single-TX Interlock and zero retry on SetPtt(true) to protect power amplifiers.
- Safe Read-Only Probe: Port detection and handshake probing is strictly non-invasive (read-only), with zero register mutations and zero TX emission.
- Antenna Rotator Control: Built-in rotctld client (TCP port 4533) rotates your antenna with a single click to the Short Path or Long Path azimuth from spots, map, or log.
- CAT Port Sharing: Built-in Hamlib proxy server (port 4534) allows external digital programs (WSJT-X, JTDX, FLDigi) to share the same radio simultaneously without port conflicts.
- HIL Test Harness: Laboratory Hardware-in-the-Loop harness requiring mandatory 50 Ω dummy load termination and strictly prohibiting PTT tests on live antennas.
title: 2. Station & CAT Setup

body:
At the core of SPLogbook is a high-performance SQLite database engine running in WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode:

- Data Integrity & Safety: WAL mode with transactional commits protects your log against corruption even during sudden power loss. Rolling automatic backups keep up to 10 historical revisions.
- High-Speed Indexing: Specialized SQLite indexes guarantee instantaneous searching and filtering even with logs exceeding ratusan thousands of QSOs.
- Smart QSO Entry Form: Automatic uppercase callsign normalization, Super Check Partial (SCP) suggestions, ITU prefix resolution, and CTY.DAT entity matching.
- Duplicate Detection: Instant visual [DUPE!] warning whenever a station has already been worked on the current band and mode.
- QSO Audio Recorder: Record live receiver audio from your soundcard and attach WAV recordings directly to individual QSO records.
- Multi-Journal Support: Maintain multiple independent logs (Home station, Club callsign, /P field activations, Contest logs).
title: 3. QSO Logging & SQLite DB

body:

- F2 — Save current QSO (Contest & DX standard)

- F11 — Toggle Fullscreen mode
- F12 — Open built-in User Manual (this window)

body:
The DX Cluster module delivers real-time DX spots and award alerts:

- Built-in Telnet Client: Connects to any DXSpider, AR-Cluster, or CC-Cluster node with automatic reconnection and live command input (e.g. sh/dx 25).
- Smart Deduplication: Sliding window filter prevents duplicate spots from flooding your table.
- Visual & Audio Alerts:
* Magenta Star (ATNO): All-Time New One DXCC entity with optional audio chime.
* Emerald Badge: New Band or New Mode for a worked DXCC country.
- Advanced Filtering: Filter by HF / WARC / VHF bands, modes (CW, SSB, FT8/FT4, Digi), continent, or hide automated RBN skimmer spots.
- Click-to-Tune: Clicking any spot tunes your transceiver VFO to the spot frequency, sets the mode, and populates the QSO entry form.
- Visual Bandmap: Real-time frequency scale displaying active stations with age-based color fading.
title: 5. DX Cluster & Bandmap

body:
SPLogbook combines real-time ionospheric modeling with live geophysical telemetry:

- Space Weather Telemetry (NOAA SWPC): Live Solar Flux Index (SFI), Sunspot Number (SSN), geomagnetic A and Kp indices, X-ray background flux, and solar wind speed.
- VOACAP-lite HF Engine: Computes great-circle midpoint, solar zenith angle, D-layer absorption, critical/maximum usable frequencies (foF2, MUF, LUF, FOT), and band opening probability (0-100%) with estimated S-meter signal level.
- Dynamic Propagation Badge: Entering a callsign immediately displays predicted circuit reliability on all HF bands.
- EME (Earth-Moon-Earth) Planner: Real-time topocentric Moon azimuth, elevation, range, Doppler shift, path loss, degradation, and mutual visibility windows.
title: 6. HF Propagation, Solar & EME

body:
SPLogbook integrates directly with external digital mode suites:

- WSJT-X / JTDX UDP Bridge (port 2237):
* Decodes binary UDP frames: Heartbeat, Status, Decode, QSO Logged, and Clear.
* Automatically logs completed FT8/FT4/JT65/Q65 QSOs with exact SNR dB reports and grid locators.
* Highlights calling stations in real time when they represent an ATNO or new band/mode.
- JS8Call (JSON TCP/UDP port 2442): Captures RX.ACTIVITY, RIG.FREQ, and LOG.QSO frames.
- FLDigi (XML-RPC port 7362): Reads frequency, mode, and QSO fields for PSK31, RTTY, Olivia, and Contestia.
- N1MM UDP Broadcasts: Emits standard XML ContactInfo packets so tools like GridTracker track your logged QSOs.
title: 7. Digital Modes (WSJT-X, JS8, FLDigi)

body:
Dedicated tools for LEO amateur satellites and the QO-100 geostationary transponder:

- SGP4/SDP4 Orbital Propagator: Uses NORAD Two-Line Elements (TLE) with one-click online updates.
- Live Orbital Telemetry: Computes azimuth, elevation, slant range, radial velocity, and ground footprint.
- Automatic CAT Doppler Correction: Continuously calculates uplink and downlink Doppler shift:
Δf = -f0 * (v_slant / c)
and updates transceiver VFO frequencies via CAT.
- Azimuth/Elevation Rotator Tracking: Drives 2-axis satellite rotators via rotctld.
title: 8. Satellite Tracking & Doppler

body:
Real-time audio spectrum analyzer and waterfall display:

- Cross-Platform Audio Capture (cpal): Captures audio directly from your transceiver USB audio codec, line-in, or virtual audio cable.
- RustFFT Engine: Fast Hann-windowed FFT computation minimizing spectral leakage.
- Configurable Controls:
* FFT sizes: 512, 1024, 2048, or 4096 bins.
* Adjustable Gain (dB), Noise Floor (dB), and Pause/Resume inspection.
* High-contrast color gradient for spotting weak CW and digital signals.
- Flexible Docking: Use inline inside the main workspace or undock to a second monitor.
title: 9. SDR Audio Spectrum & Waterfall

Comprehensive data exchange and cloud logbook synchronization:

- ADIF 3.1.5 & ADX: Full import/export compatibility with standard .adi and XML .adx files.
- Online Logbooks: Direct two-way or upload synchronization with ARRL LoTW (via TQSL), eQSL.cc, Club Log, QRZ.com Logbook, HamQTH, Cloudlog, and HRDLog.net.

body:
Extend SPLogbook safely with sandboxed user scripts:

- Rhai Scripting Sandbox: Write custom .rhai plugins without recompiling the application. Strict operation and memory limits keep the UI responsive.
- Lifecycle Hooks: on_startup(), on_qso_logged(call, band, mode, freq, is_atno), on_dx_spot(spotter, call, freq, comment), on_rig_state(freq, mode, connected), and on_band_opened(band).
- Command Bridge: Scripts can trigger CW macros, voice keyer messages, rotator headings, audio alerts, and QSO fields.
- Built-in Plugin Marketplace: One-click installation of curated plugins (POTA Helper, CW Macros, Contest Assistant, Rotor Assistant, Band Activity Logger).

body:
Secure multi-station Host/Peer operation over a local LAN or private VPN tunnel:

- Host/Peer Architecture: One station operates as Host (listening on a chosen TCP port, default 7373), while other stations connect as Peers by specifying the Host IP/hostname and port.
- Authenticated Encryption: All network frames are encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305. Session keys are derived via Argon2id from a random salt and shared secret. Passwords are never transmitted in plaintext.
- Replay and Reorder Protection: Every frame includes a monotonic counter and unique identifier, preventing replay and reordering attacks.
- Catch-up Inventory Replication: Upon establishing an authenticated session, stations exchange SHA-256 journal inventories and checksums for the active journal, automatically transferring missing QSOs bidirectionally without duplicates.
- Status Diagnostics & Reconnect: The Multi-Op window displays live connection status (Listening, Connected, Reconnecting, Error). Clear errors indicate bad secrets ('Invalid password or secret') or protocol version mismatches ('Unsupported protocol version'). If network connectivity is lost, Peers automatically attempt reconnection every 5 seconds.
- Synchronization Boundaries & Limitations:
* Sync operates strictly on the active journal.
* Only new QSO additions are synchronized; edits and deletions are not propagated across peers.
* Designed for trusted local networks (LAN) or secure private VPN tunnels. Direct exposure to the public Internet without VPN is not recommended.
* Ensure the firewall permits inbound TCP traffic on the configured port (default 7373).
title: 15. Encrypted Multi-Op Sync (LAN/VPN)

body:
SPLogbook runs natively on 64-bit Windows 10/11 and GNU/Linux. Key platform notes:

GNU/Linux (x86_64):
1. USB Serial Port Permissions:
Add your user account to the serial group to access /dev/ttyUSB* and /dev/ttyACM*:
- Debian / Ubuntu / Mint / Raspberry Pi OS:
sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER
- Arch / Manjaro / Fedora / openSUSE:
sudo usermod -aG uucp $USER
Log out and log back in after running the command.
2. Data Directories (XDG Standard):
- Databases & logs: ~/.local/share/splogbook/
- Configuration: ~/.config/splogbook/

Microsoft Windows (10 / 11 64-bit):
1. Virtual COM Ports: Install the transceiver manufacturer's USB UART driver (Silicon Labs CP210x, FTDI, or CH340) and select the detected COM port in CAT Settings.
2. Windows Firewall: Allow SPLogbook on private networks when using the WSJT-X UDP bridge (2237), CAT proxy (4534), or Multi-Op LAN sync.
3. Data Directory: Stored in %APPDATA%\SPLogbook\
title: 16. Windows & Linux Setup

body:
Solutions to common technical questions:

Q: My transceiver does not connect via CAT.
A: 1. Ensure no other program (WSJT-X, OmniRig, Putty) is holding the same COM/tty serial port open.
2. Verify that the Baud Rate in CAT Settings matches your radio's menu setting (e.g. 38400 or 115200).
3. In Serial mode, enable 'Auto-start rigctld' or choose the direct Kenwood/Icom backend.

Q: Clicking 'Update Online Database' — how do I know it finished?
A: SPLogbook downloads the latest CTY.DAT, MASTER.SCP, and LoTW user activity list in the background, reloads them immediately into memory, and shows a confirmation toast notification.

Q: DX Cluster disconnects immediately after connecting.
A: DXSpider and AR-Cluster nodes require a valid amateur callsign at login. Set your callsign in Station Settings (if left as N0CALL, SPLogbook automatically uses a fallback guest callsign).

Q: Can I move my logbook database to another computer?
A: Yes! Click 'Open Data Directory' below and copy your .db file (or create a ZIP backup in the Backup Manager). SQLite files are 100% compatible across Windows and Linux.
